item.title: Kerry lose at home to Waterford
item.description: Kerry have been beaten in the Lidl Ladies National Football League. Advertisement They went down to Waterford in Fitzgerald Stadium, Killarney, the visitors winning 2-12 to 1-11. Bríd McMaugh struck 1-4 as Waterford made it two wins on the bounce. The teams came into the game with success on the road in Round 1 with Kerry overcoming Dublin in pretty rough conditions and Waterford having the better of Armagh. item.title: Gold Cup victory for Fact To File
item.description: Willie Mullins Galopin Des Champs did not make it four in a row in the Paddy Power Irish Gold Cup at Leopardstown. The ten year old finished third behind Fact To File in first and Gaelic Warrior in second. The first Grade One on today's card, the Novice Hurdle, went the way of 'Doctor Steinburg'. item.title: England captain named on bench for six nations opener
item.description: England captain Maro Itoje has been named on the bench for their six nations opener against Wales this weekend The 31-year-old has missed training due to the recent passing of his mother. Jamie George will lead the side in his place at Twickenham on Saturday. Advertisement

item.title: 8% of Kerry adults are regularly vaping
item.description: 8% of adults in Kerry are vaping. That's according to research by the Respect Vapers group, who are claiming that 9,717 adults in the Kingdom vape, with 4,859 using the habit to quit smoking. New government legislation on the sale of vapes and e-cigarettes includes the restriction of flavoured vapes and liquids. item.title: Safety concerns raised over bridge missing from repair priority list
item.description: Serious safety concerns have been raised about a key bridge serving South Kerry, after councillors questioned why it does not appear on Kerry County Council’s priority list for bridge repairs. At the January full council meeting, councillor Maura Healy-Rae said Loo Bridge on the R569 near Poulgorm junction is deteriorating rapidly, has been struck several times by vehicles, and can no longer cope with the volume of traffic using the route.
